task: Cover the order tracking page (`/`). The timeline lists five steps (Ordered, Packed, Shipped, Out for delivery, Delivered); exactly one step is marked Current, the earlier ones Done and the later ones Upcoming, and the header line reads `Step N of 5: <step name>`. The Advance (test seam) button moves the order to the next step. Cancel order is offered only while the order has not reached Shipped; cancelling shows `Order cancelled` in the header and the `Cancelled` notice, hides the estimated delivery, and leaves no step marked Current. Progress and cancellation are stored on the server and survive a reload.

faults.brief_phrase: The Advance (test seam) button moves the order to the next step
faults.description: Advance sends the request but the page does not change until a reload.
faults.replace:
const next = await api("POST", "/api/dev/advance");
      void next;

faults.brief_phrase: exactly one step is marked Current
faults.description: After an advance the previous step stays marked Current as well.
faults.find:
if (index < state.step) status = "Done";
          else if (index === state.step) status = "Current";
faults.replace:
if (index < state.step - 1) status = "Done";
          else if (index <= state.step) status = "Current";

faults.brief_phrase: the header line reads `Step N of 5: <step name>`
faults.description: The header keeps `Step 1 of 5: Ordered` while the timeline advances.
faults.find: el("ot-header").textContent = state.cancelled ? "Order cancelled" : "Step " + state.step + " of " + STEPS.length + ": " + STEPS[state.step - 1];
faults.replace: el("ot-header").textContent = state.cancelled ? "Order cancelled" : "Step 1 of " + STEPS.length + ": " + STEPS[0];

faults.brief_phrase: Cancel order is offered only while the order has not reached Shipped
faults.description: Cancel order is still shown at the Shipped step (the server then refuses it).

faults.brief_phrase: Progress and cancellation are stored on the server and survive a reload
faults.description: The server answers with the next step but does not store it; a reload shows the previous step.
faults.find:
if (order.step < STEPS.length) order.step += 1;
      return json(res, 200, order);
